items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: There was a toe dancer, one of the first black toe dancers I ever saw in my life by the name of Mary Richards.

ctx.x: Apex or the Alabam who were -- I think we were talking about the Apex -- who were known mostly only on the West Coast.

Oh, in those old days, there were singers like a fellow they called Strut Mitchell. He was a singer and a dancer. There were lady singers and dancers like, for instance, there was a girl by the name of May Ellix (PHONETIC) out of Chicago, very beautiful, attractive woman, that sang and danced. There was Sue Hoy (PHONETIC) and there was Martha Richie (PHONETIC) and Baby Mack. Baby Mack was Les Height's wife. Baby Mack Height.
